companies.name: Synopsys
companies.thesis_note: Half of the EDA duopoly, and the layer every chip on this map passes through before it exists. The moat is switching cost compounded over decades — flows, libraries, IP and engineer muscle memory — plus a licence model that converts design-start growth into recurring revenue with no fab risk. AI chip complexity increases tool intensity per design, and Synopsys' own AI-assisted design tools raise it further. 2026 state: down ~38% from the high on China-licence uncertainty rather than demand. Risk: export controls are an on/off switch Washington can flip without warning.
companies.froth_note: Duopoly royalty model, no AI capex sensitivity in earnings; July selloff barely touched it.

companies.name: Cadence Design Systems
companies.thesis_note: The other half of the EDA duopoly, with the stronger position in emulation and prototyping (Palladium) — the hardware that verifies a design before anyone commits to a $100M+ mask set. As AI chips grow past reticle limits and into multi-die packages, verification becomes the binding constraint on schedule, which is exactly where Cadence's advantage sits. Recurring, high-margin, fab-free. 2026 state: down ~19% and carrying the same China-licence overhang as Synopsys. Risk: the duopoly is stable, but policy is not.
companies.froth_note: Same duopoly economics as SNPS; valuation full but earnings are subscription-anchored.

companies.name: Arm Holdings
companies.thesis_note: The dominant CPU instruction-set architecture — a royalty on nearly every phone shipped and a growing share of datacenter CPUs, including Nvidia's Grace and Vera companions and the hyperscalers' in-house designs. The economics are pure toll: no fabs, no inventory, revenue per chip regardless of who wins the socket. 2026 state: datacenter share is genuinely inflecting. Risk: the highest-froth name in the conviction-3 tier — the multiple prices decades of share gain, and the Arm China joint venture remains a governance wrinkle nobody has cleanly resolved.
companies.froth_note: Royalty moat is real but the multiple prices decades of datacenter share gains — classic priced-for-perfection.

companies.name: Empyrean Technology
companies.thesis_note: China's leading EDA firm; cannot match full-flow leading-edge but the national champion under sanctions pressure.

companies.name: ASML Holding
companies.thesis_note: Sole maker of EUV lithography — the single deepest chokepoint in technology. No advanced logic or DRAM node exists without it, and the machine cannot be cloned: Zeiss (private) supplies optics no one else can polish, Trumpf (private) the drive lasers, and the systems-integration knowledge is decades deep. High-NA is now validated in production at Intel's 18A, which extends the roadmap another decade. 2026 state: beat and guided above consensus in July and the stock sold off anyway. Risks are political and cyclical, not competitive — China demand normalising, order lumpiness, and the fact that a monopoly with a backlog still trades on the tape's mood.
companies.froth_note: Monopoly + record Q2 beat SOLD OFF in July — sentiment inversion compressed an already reasonable multiple. Entry-window profile.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.thesis_note: The broadest wafer-fab equipment portfolio (~18% share) — deposition, etch, ion implant, CMP, and increasingly the hybrid-bonding tools that advanced packaging runs on. Breadth is the moat: Applied touches nearly every process step, so it captures spend regardless of which node or memory type wins, and the installed-base service annuity compounds beneath the capex cycle. 2026 state: the AI fab build-out is expanding while Chinese localisation demand rolls over — a mix shift that has compressed the multiple more than the earnings. Risk: a China-wide equipment ban would cut the remaining backlog outright.
companies.froth_note: Broad WFE at market-like multiple; capex spine (~$700B hyperscaler + TSMC $60-64B) underwrites the backlog.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.thesis_note: Etch + deposition leader; critical for 3D NAND and gate-all-around. China exposure a swing factor.
companies.froth_note: Etch/deposition duopolist down ~27% into an HBM capex cycle it directly levers — the July selloff did this one a favour.

companies.name: KLA Corporation
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in process control — the inspection and metrology that decides whether a wafer yields. Yield is the gating economic variable at every new node, which makes KLA structurally counter-cyclical in importance: the harder the node, the more inspection intensity per wafer. Incremental margins above 60% follow from that pricing power. 2026 state: HBM stacking and advanced packaging add whole new inspection steps, and the stock still sits ~35% off its high. Risk: a capex digestion phase pauses process-control spend first, and China is a meaningful share of the base.
companies.froth_note: Process-control near-monopoly; premium multiple but earned by 60%+ incremental margins.

companies.name: Tokyo Electron
companies.thesis_note: Japan's WFE champion; coat/develop (with ASML litho) + etch/deposition. Core to every fab line.
companies.froth_note: Broadest Japanese WFE franchise at a 30% drawdown; China exposure is the risk the price is arguing about, not AI demand.

companies.name: VAT Group
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in the vacuum valves inside essentially every deposition and etch chamber on earth. A component nobody outside the industry can name, single-sourced into tools that cost tens of millions, where a valve failure idles the whole chamber — so qualification is sticky and price sensitivity is low. This is the purest expression of the dashboard's thesis: the value sits with the irreplaceable component, not the branded tool. 2026 state: still priced as a Swiss industrial rather than an AI chokepoint. Risk: it is a pure WFE-cycle instrument with no diversification.
companies.froth_note: Vacuum-valve chokepoint nobody prices for AI; froth simply hasn't reached it.

companies.name: Advantest
companies.thesis_note: One half of the automated-test-equipment duopoly with Teradyne, and the half levered to complexity. HBM stacks and multi-die AI packages lengthen test time per device, so Advantest's revenue rises with difficulty rather than merely with unit volume — and HBM4's triple qualification means three suppliers each running full qualification programmes. 2026 state: a violent re-rating on that logic (up 16% in a single session in August). Risk: the multiple now assumes test intensity keeps compounding; a memory-capex pause hits test first.
companies.froth_note: HBM/SoC test monopoly-ish, but the stock became a momentum favorite — multiple carries AI premium.

companies.name: MKS Instruments
companies.thesis_note: Process subsystems (gas, vacuum, RF, lasers) + advanced packaging chemistry (Atotech). Broad WFE+packaging exposure.
companies.froth_note: Subsystem chokepoint (vacuum, RF, photonics) at a subsystem multiple; leverage on the balance sheet is the caveat, not the story.

companies.name: NAURA Technology
companies.thesis_note: China's largest WFE maker (~#8 globally); etch/deposition/clean. The localization bellwether ex-lithography.

companies.name: ASM International
companies.thesis_note: Leader in Atomic Layer Deposition — the gating process for the FinFET→GAAFET (nanosheet) transition (film conformality on 3D surfaces). Underappreciated vs ASML/AMAT; ALD steps rise sharply at GAA nodes. Owns ~25% of ASMPT.
companies.froth_note: ALD leadership matters more with every gate-all-around node; a 25% drawdown on a monopoly-adjacent position.

companies.name: Onto Innovation
companies.thesis_note: Process control / metrology + advanced-packaging inspection; HBM and chiplet complexity drives more inspection steps per wafer. Smaller semicap leveraged to the AI/HBM capex cycle.
companies.froth_note: Inspection/metrology levered to HBM stacking yields — the quiet way to own the qualification cycle.

companies.name: AIXTRON
companies.thesis_note: MOCVD monopoly (70-90% share; >85% GaN) — grows the III-V epi layers behind every photonics laser AND the GaN power devices for 800V HVDC. Dual photonics + GaN tailwind the market underprices. A hidden German chokepoint.
companies.froth_note: MOCVD monopoly still priced as a cyclical German mid-cap; GaN/photonics optionality free.

companies.name: SUSS MicroTec
companies.thesis_note: Near-monopoly in photomask cleaning (~90% at TSMC) + ~50% of Samsung/Micron HBM temp bonding; its XBS300 does the laser-to-wafer heterogeneous integration every SiPh foundry (GFS/Tower/UMC) needs, plus hybrid bonding. ~70% of revenue is advanced packaging.
companies.froth_note: Hetero-integration tooling at industrial-company multiple.

companies.name: Veeco Instruments
companies.thesis_note: The only credible MOCVD competitor to AIXTRON (together a duopoly) — III-V epi for photonics + GaN power; also laser annealing / ion beam. Mid-merger with EV-exposed Axcelis (ACLS); weaker setup than AIXTRON but cheap optionality.

companies.name: Wonik IPS
companies.thesis_note: Korean front-end deposition equipment maker; GEMINI PECVD platform used in Samsung 3nm GAA + 2nm logic process. ~50% revenue from Samsung Electronics. Tool move-in happens BEFORE wafer revenue — early-cycle beneficiary of Samsung's Taylor (TX) leading-edge build-out + memory P4/P5/M15X/Yongin investment cycle.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.thesis_note: The keystone. Effectively all leading-edge AI logic is fabricated here, and CoWoS packaging capacity gates how many accelerators the world can physically ship — roughly 1M wafers of 2026 demand already booked with Nvidia holding ~60%. Replicating it needs a decade, $100B+, and a workforce that does not exist elsewhere, which is why customer concentration cuts in TSMC's favour rather than against it. 2026 state: record Q2, capex raised to $60–64B, N2 ramping, and the stock fell on capex fear. Risk: Taiwan concentration is the tail risk overlaying the entire dashboard.
companies.froth_note: Record Q2, raised capex, stock FELL — the July shakeout's cleanest quality-at-a-discount case.

companies.name: Samsung Electronics
companies.thesis_note: Only IDM spanning DRAM/HBM/NAND + foundry + OLEDoS. Samsung Foundry is being repriced as the most realistic global second source for leading-edge logic — Tesla's $16.5B Taylor 1 deal anchors a 2H27 ramp; Taylor 2 in active 2nm review; Marvell's Google memory-adjacent ASIC slotted on Samsung 4nm (mid-2027 launch). HBM4 qual recovery is the memory leg. Jul 2026: HBM4 mass production (started Feb) now feeding an estimated 25-30% of Vera Rubin volume — the Korea-Unlocked re-rating thesis progressing.
companies.froth_note: Conglomerate discount persists while HBM4 qualification and the foundry second-source thesis both turn — the widest gap between narrative and price in memory.

companies.name: Intel
companies.thesis_note: High-NA EUV lead customer (14A). US foundry turnaround optionality; execution + external-customer wins are the swing.

companies.name: UMC
companies.thesis_note: Mature-node foundry; display drivers, RF, power. Exposed to China mature-node overcapacity but stable cash flows.
companies.froth_note: Mature-node pessimism is fully priced; the imec silicon-photonics work is an unpaid-for option.

companies.name: GlobalFoundries
companies.thesis_note: US/EU specialty foundry — automotive, RF, power. Western-supply-security premium; not leading-edge.
companies.froth_note: Down ~42% on mature-node softness while the SiPh/GaN franchise builds — cheap relative to what it owns.

companies.name: SMIC
companies.thesis_note: China's foundry champion; 7nm via DUV multipatterning powers Huawei Ascend. Capped at ~7nm by export controls.

companies.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
companies.thesis_note: Largest 300mm wafer maker (with SUMCO ~50%+); also photoresist. Quiet upstream Japan chokepoint under TSMC itself.
companies.froth_note: Half of the world's 300mm wafer supply at a specialty-chemicals multiple; the least AI-priced monopoly in the map.

companies.name: SUMCO
companies.thesis_note: Second 300mm wafer giant. AI capacity ramp tightens wafer supply; pure-play wafer cycle exposure.

companies.name: Siltronic
companies.thesis_note: German pure-play silicon wafer maker — fourth in the global 300mm cohort behind Shin-Etsu/SUMCO/GlobalWafers. EU Chips Act 2.0 + AI wafer-cycle exposure.

companies.name: GlobalWafers
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan's wafer champion — ~17% global share (2025), third-largest behind Shin-Etsu + SUMCO. Spun out of Sino-American Silicon; 18 sites in 9 countries incl. Sherman, TX (CHIPS-Act). Sells to TSMC + TI directly.
companies.froth_note: Wafer oligopoly economics after a ~43% drawdown — supply discipline matters more than the AI narrative here.

companies.name: National Silicon Industry Group (NSIG)
companies.thesis_note: China's silicon-wafer national champion — 200mm + 300mm + SOI from Shanghai STAR (IPO 2020). The China-domestic wafer-cycle play; localization beneficiary as fabs ramp.

companies.name: AXT Inc
companies.thesis_note: Compound-semi substrate maker (InP, GaAs, Ge) — China-based production directly affected by InP export controls. June 2026 China InP-export easing is a direct catalyst: unlocks upstream photonics substrate bottleneck. Small but the cleanest US-listed InP-easing beneficiary.

companies.name: Soitec
companies.thesis_note: ~80% of silicon-on-insulator wafers — the substrate every photonic IC (incl. TSMC COUPE) is built on; Shin-Etsu licenses its Smart Cut. Priced as a mobile/RF cyclical; SiPh + LNOI/SmartSiC is the underpriced optionality. Cross-link to Optical.
companies.froth_note: SOI substrate monopoly at depressed multiple (mobile drag masks the photonics/POI story).

companies.name: Tower Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Specialty analog/RF/power foundry investing ~$650M to triple silicon-photonics shipments by mid-2026 — a SiPh-foundry beneficiary of the CPO wave alongside GFS/UMC. Geographically diversified.

companies.name: SK Hynix
companies.thesis_note: HBM leader (~62%), Nvidia's lead supplier; MR-MUF process edge. The single best pure-play on the HBM bottleneck. Jul 2026: holds an estimated 60-70% of Vera Rubin HBM4 volume (all three suppliers qualified — a first for any HBM generation); Rubin ships Q3.
companies.froth_note: HBM leadership intact but July proved LTA structure caps upside surprise — repriced, not broken. Watch HBM4 Q3 ramp.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.thesis_note: Only US memory maker; HBM3E ramp overtook Samsung (~21%). US-supply-security + HBM growth dual thesis. Jul 2026: qualified + in production for Vera Rubin HBM4 alongside SKH/Samsung — first triple-qualified HBM generation; 36GB 12H HVM confirmed at GTC. Aug 2026 re-rank 3→2: HBM4 is the first triple-qualified generation — with all three suppliers shipping Rubin and LTAs capping price upside, per-supplier chokepoint power is diluted; MU holds the smallest Rubin share. Thesis intact, chokepoint claim weakened.
companies.froth_note: Rides the same HBM tide with more commodity-DRAM beta; historically the froth transmission channel in memory.

companies.name: Kioxia Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Japan NAND leader (ex-Toshiba); relisted on the TSE Prime Market Dec 2024 (ticker 285A). NAND cycle + AI storage tier; HBM-era enterprise-SSD demand.

companies.name: SanDisk
companies.thesis_note: WD NAND spinoff; enterprise SSD + AI storage. Commoditized but cyclical-leverage play.

companies.name: Phison Electronics
companies.thesis_note: Controller leader; AI inference local-storage + memory-expansion angle. Taiwan-listed controller pure-play.

companies.name: ASE Technology
companies.thesis_note: World's largest OSAT (~45% of top-10); CoWoS overflow + advanced packaging ramp. Direct AI packaging leverage.
companies.froth_note: World #1 OSAT at a mid-teens drawdown and an unremarkable multiple — the CoWoS overflow beneficiary the market treats as commodity.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.thesis_note: #2 OSAT; $7B Arizona advanced-packaging fab with Apple/TSMC — the US back-end reshoring play.
companies.froth_note: Down ~40% with the Arizona fab and TSMC/Apple relationships intact; priced as cyclical OSAT, not as reshoring infrastructure.

companies.name: BE Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: The hybrid-bonding equipment leader — the tooling that stacks dies at sub-10µm pitch without solder, which is how HBM4E and future 3D logic get built. Bonding accuracy is the physical limit on stacking density, and the qualification cycle with memory makers takes years, so leadership here converts directly into the next memory generation's economics. 2026 state: the HBM4E hybrid-bonding transition is the whole story. Risk: the multiple assumes that roadmap arrives on schedule; TCB incumbents are defending hard.
companies.froth_note: Hybrid-bonding story widely owned; multiple assumes the roadmap executes on schedule.

companies.name: ASMPT
companies.thesis_note: Bonders + advanced packaging tools (TCB, hybrid bonding). Leveraged to the packaging capex cycle.
companies.froth_note: Hybrid-bonding tool leadership is the right thing to own; the multiple assumes the roadmap arrives on schedule.

companies.name: Ibiden
companies.thesis_note: Top ABF substrate maker; high-layer-count substrates for big AI dies are supply-constrained. Japan substrate chokepoint.
companies.froth_note: ABF substrate oligopolist down ~41% into a substrate shortage — one of the cleanest dislocations in the map.

companies.name: Unimicron
companies.thesis_note: ABF substrate leader (~22%). AI-die substrate demand + capacity tightness. Taiwan substrate pure-play.
companies.froth_note: Substrate capacity is tight and this is the liquid way to own it; the market rates it accordingly.

companies.name: Ajinomoto
companies.thesis_note: Makes the Ajinomoto Build-up Film that insulates essentially every IC substrate in the world — a near-monopoly upstream of a named bottleneck, sitting inside a food and amino-acid company. The market prices seasoning; the film is unreplicated because qualification runs through every substrate maker and every packaging house simultaneously. 2026 state: substrate capacity remains effectively sold out, and the stock is ~21% off its high. Risk: the conglomerate discount is perennial — the value has been obvious for years without unlocking.
companies.froth_note: ABF film monopoly buried inside a food company — the market still doesn't price it as semis.

companies.name: Kulicke & Soffa
companies.thesis_note: Bonding equipment; advanced packaging + thermocompression transition. Cyclical assembly-capex exposure.

companies.name: FormFactor
companies.thesis_note: Near-duopoly (with Micronics Japan) in MEMS probe cards that contact thousands of 40µm-pitch HBM microbumps for known-good-die screening — the hardest test in the industry. Nvidia tightening HBM test standards is a direct tailwind.
companies.froth_note: HBM test-card chokepoint at a modest multiple; quietly geared to every HBM4 qual.

companies.name: Powertech (PTI)
companies.thesis_note: Memory back-end (DRAM/HBM/NAND test, near-full utilization) + PiFO — a leading CoWoS-L alternative — and FOPLP; >NT$40bn 2026 capex; Meta reportedly interested in PiFO. A second-source advanced-packaging play as CoWoS stays tight.
companies.froth_note: Memory test plus PiFO packaging optionality at a modest multiple after a ~36% drawdown.

companies.name: Cohu
companies.thesis_note: Automated test handlers + the Neon HBM inspection tool + Eclipse handler (active thermal control for ~3,000W AI processors). Leveraged to AI-chip + HBM test complexity; cyclical.

companies.name: Hanmi Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: ~90% share of HBM4 thermo-compression (TCB) bonders — a Korea HBM-packaging chokepoint. But the HBM4E→HBM5 shift to hybrid bonding (BESI/ASMPT) is a structural risk; SK Hynix co-developing 2nd-gen hybrid tools with Hanwha. A chokepoint-at-risk.

companies.name: Doosan Tesna
companies.thesis_note: Korea's #1 system-semi wafer-test OSAT; revenue scales with Samsung Foundry utilization. KRW171.4bn capex for Apple CIS line (2H26) + KRW190.9bn for Nvidia LPU package-level test (Q4 2026 ramp) + Pyeongtaek Plant 2 shell (Nov 2027) sized for Marvell's Google-bound 2nm ASIC. AI-infra cycle replacing the mobile cycle.

companies.name: Samsung Electro-Mechanics
companies.thesis_note: Dual thesis: (1) FC-BGA captive substrate vendor for Samsung Foundry — every new 4nm/3nm/2nm chip accumulates SKUs here; industry-wide FC-BGA capacity tight. (2) MLCC content per Rubin Ultra ~1.8M units (~90x H100); 24-week lead times; the 800V-DC transition adds ultra-high-voltage MLCC demand (>10x ASP premium). Top-tier alongside Murata, TDK, Taiyo Yuden.
companies.froth_note: Deepest drawdown in the packaging complex (~48%) across FC-BGA substrates and MLCC — Korean discount on genuine AI content.

companies.name: LG Innotek
companies.thesis_note: SiP (System-in-Package) substrates for smartphones/wearables/TWS/AR-VR. Survivor-economics play: every major substrate maker is reallocating capacity toward AI-server FC-BGA, leaving SiP undersupplied — same pattern as MLC NAND (Macronix) and DDR4 (Nanya). Margins could lift from ~9.5% (2026) toward ~14% (2028).

companies.name: Aehr Test Systems
companies.thesis_note: Burn-in test specialist — stresses chips at heat to filter infant-mortality defects. Google placed a $41M follow-on TPU package-level burn-in order (FY27 deliveries) — first hyperscale-AI design-in. Sonoma (package) + FOX (wafer) platforms; future vectors: SiC, GaN, flash, HBM, silicon photonics. Insurance policy on very expensive silicon.
companies.froth_note: Micro-cap near its high on a burn-in narrative levered to a handful of customer decisions.

companies.name: Nvidia
companies.thesis_note: ~80-90% merchant AI silicon; CUDA moat; Blackwell→Rubin. Also NVLink, BlueField DPU, Jetson Thor, $4B optics. The hub. Jul 2026: Vera Rubin in full production, Q3 shipping; 288GB HBM4 per GPU across 8 stacks; Spectrum-X CPO switch shipping to select partners.
companies.froth_note: Fundamentals keep delivering, but it IS the AI trade — any capex-ROI wobble reprices it first. Custom-ASIC share shift is the structural watch item.

companies.name: Advanced Micro Devices
companies.thesis_note: MI300→MI400 (HBM4, 2nm) + Helios rack; the credible #2 merchant accelerator. ROCm software is the gating risk.
companies.froth_note: Real MI-series revenue, but the 'credible Nvidia challenger' premium survives every drawdown — you pay for the narrative as well as the units.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.thesis_note: The custom-ASIC and networking franchise: co-designs Google's TPU, Meta's MTIA and OpenAI's accelerator (a ~$10B programme starting late 2026), while also supplying the merchant switch silicon most AI clusters route through, plus a co-packaged-optics position now in mass production. Broadcom monetises the counter-trend to Nvidia and the network that any accelerator needs — two ways to win from the same build-out. 2026 state: every custom-silicon announcement confirms the thesis. Risk: it is consensus, and ASIC programmes can be reassigned.
companies.froth_note: Custom-ASIC + networking momentum (OpenAI $10B) is confirmation — and consensus; premium multiple with real earnings behind it.

companies.name: Marvell Technology
companies.thesis_note: AWS Trainium + Microsoft Maia ASICs + optical DSP. Nvidia took a stake around NVLink Fusion. Custom-silicon #2.
companies.froth_note: Custom-ASIC #2 narrative owns the multiple; execution against AVGO is the risk.

companies.name: Alchip Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Turnkey backend ASIC design at advanced nodes (AWS et al.). Taiwan picks-and-shovels on the custom-ASIC wave.
companies.froth_note: Custom-ASIC design services already de-rated ~40% from the high; the ASIC story is intact but the multiple still assumes it wins share.

companies.name: Global Unichip (GUC)
companies.thesis_note: TSMC-affiliated ASIC design service; advanced-node turnkey. Leverage to custom AI silicon proliferation.

companies.name: Cambricon
companies.thesis_note: China AI-chip champion; benefits from domestic-compute mandate + Nvidia export curbs. Capped by SMIC/HBM access.

companies.name: MediaTek
companies.thesis_note: Co-designs Google's TPU v7 (Trillium) — a custom-ASIC co-design win beyond the AVGO/MRVL duo; underappreciated AI leverage after weak mobile. Top mobile/edge SoC vendor.
companies.froth_note: Handset base funds the company; the TPU co-design angle is close to a free option at a mid-teens drawdown.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.thesis_note: Ethernet leader for AI back-end networks; Ultra Ethernet beneficiary vs InfiniBand. Hyperscaler-concentrated.
companies.froth_note: At its high; the best-in-class AI-networking franchise with a multiple that requires it to stay best-in-class against Broadcom-based white boxes.

companies.name: Astera Labs
companies.thesis_note: PCIe/CXL retimers + fabric switches + AECs — the AI-connectivity pure-play; UALink optionality. Premium valuation.
companies.froth_note: Even 25% off the high, the multiple prices near-flawless execution on connectivity content per GPU.

companies.name: Credo Technology
companies.thesis_note: ZeroFlap AECs dominant top-of-rack; signal-integrity at 224G. High-growth connectivity niche.
companies.froth_note: Same profile as Astera: real content growth, valuation that assumes the copper-reach window stays open.

companies.name: SiTime
companies.thesis_note: MEMS timing/oscillators inside 1.6T modules, NICs, switches and accelerator boards — content ~doubles to ~$2/module at 1.6T, ~25-50% of a growing TAM. Exclusive MEMS-oscillator supplier for Apple's in-house 5G modem. Architecture-agnostic AI-timing play.
companies.froth_note: MEMS timing content per rack is rising; a small-cap premium name that swings hard on single-quarter guidance.

companies.name: Celestica
companies.thesis_note: Hyperscaler white-box networking + AI server ODM. Cheaper torque on the cluster-fabric buildout.
companies.froth_note: An ODM that re-rated to a growth multiple on AI mix — the earnings are real, the re-rating assumes they persist.

companies.name: Accton Technology
companies.thesis_note: Leading white-box switch ODM for hyperscalers. Taiwan networking-hardware pure-play.

companies.name: Cisco Systems
companies.thesis_note: Networking incumbent; SiliconOne G300 (102.4 Tbps) switch silicon + AgenticOps/Splunk observability. Beneficiary of the agentic 'east-west' traffic surge + enterprise-networking refresh, though less AI-pure than Arista.

companies.name: Hon Hai (Foxconn)
companies.thesis_note: Largest AI-server/rack assembler; GB200 NVL72 builds. Scale leader; thin margins but huge AI revenue ramp.
companies.froth_note: The largest AI-server revenue base in the world at an assembler's multiple — the market still prices Foxconn as iPhone assembly.

companies.name: Quanta Computer
companies.thesis_note: Major AI-server ODM; rev +66% YoY. Direct beneficiary of hyperscaler GPU-server demand.
companies.froth_note: Same picture as Hon Hai with a higher AI mix: strong revenue growth, valuation still anchored to contract-manufacturing norms.

companies.name: Wiwynn
companies.thesis_note: ~50% of hyperscale AI-server procurement; rev +149% YoY. The purest Taiwan AI-server ODM play.
companies.froth_note: At its 52-week high as the purest hyperscale-ODM play — the AI-server narrative is fully in this price.

companies.name: Super Micro Computer
companies.thesis_note: US AI-server leader; liquid-cooled rack-scale. Governance/accounting overhang is the key risk to weigh.
companies.froth_note: Share-gain story with accounting history and Dell/HPE closing in; froth concentrates in it every rally.

companies.name: Vertiv Holdings
companies.thesis_note: The systems layer of datacenter power and thermal — UPS, busway, cooling distribution units and the liquid-cooling architecture that rack-scale AI now mandates rather than merely prefers. Vertiv sells the constraint: as racks move past 100kW, cooling and power delivery become the limiting factor on how much compute a building can hold. 2026 state: attach rates keep rising and the order book reflects it. Risk: the crowd's favourite picks-and-shovels name, so it trades with sentiment flows as much as with fundamentals.
companies.froth_note: The crowd's favorite picks-and-shovels; July 16 rotation hit it despite intact fundamentals — froth flows in and out of this one fast.

companies.name: Delta Electronics
companies.thesis_note: World-leading DC power supplies + power management; 48V-to-chip transition. Quiet AI-power compounder. Jul 2026: named manufacturing partner behind Broadcom's 51.2T Bailly CPO switch volume ramp — a second AI leg beyond PSUs. Aug 2026 re-rank 2→3: three confirmations stacked — PSU/power-shelf leadership into the 800V-DC transition (first volume shipments due Q3), named Bailly CPO manufacturing partner, and MLCC-to-rack power breadth. Delta is becoming the AI-power chokepoint.

companies.name: Monolithic Power
companies.thesis_note: Power-management silicon for GPU boards; content-per-GPU rising with 1kW+ accelerators. High-quality compounder.
companies.froth_note: Genuine power-IC content growth per accelerator, but the multiple has long assumed continued share gains at Nvidia.

companies.name: Asia Vital Components
companies.thesis_note: Cold plates + thermal modules for AI servers; liquid-cooling ramp. Taiwan cooling pure-play.
companies.froth_note: Cooling content per rack is rising fast; the stock has already re-rated to reflect the liquid transition.

companies.name: GE Vernova
companies.thesis_note: Gas turbines + grid for behind-the-meter AI power. The cross-link from datacenters into the energy supply chain.
companies.froth_note: Turbine backlog is real and sold out; the AI-power narrative has done most of the work in the multiple.

companies.name: Wolfspeed
companies.thesis_note: Pure-play silicon carbide; runs the world's only commercial 200mm SiC fab (Mohawk Valley) + demoed the first 300mm SiC crystal (only Coherent is close). Post-Ch.11, debt-free — levered to 800V-DC AI racks inheriting the EV/solar SiC supply chain. Turnaround risk.
companies.froth_note: NOT a froth case — a balance-sheet case. Down ~63%, the question is solvency and SiC pricing, not whether the story is over-owned.

companies.name: onsemi
companies.thesis_note: Broad-line SiC + silicon power; EV/solar capacity now finding a second AI-datacenter cohort (800V HVDC). Also a CMOS image-sensor maker (robotics/auto). Valued on the soft EV cycle.
companies.froth_note: Cyclical trough valuation with SiC capacity in place; the 800V transition is upside the price does not demand.

companies.name: STMicroelectronics
companies.thesis_note: European IDM; SiC power + analog/MCU. 'Supply-chain inheritance' play — EV-validated wide-bandgap capacity now serving AI power. Also a silicon-photonics play: its PIC100 platform (TSV + SiPh) anchors a multi-year, multi-billion AWS datacenter-optics + laser-driver contract. Diversified, EV-cycle exposed.
companies.froth_note: Analog/SiC at a low-teens multiple with European-industrial pessimism baked in; SiPh and 800V content are free options.

companies.name: Navitas Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Pure-play GaN (+SiC) for high-frequency power conversion; GlobalFoundries-partnered and aligned to Nvidia's 800V-DC architecture. Small, volatile, high-beta on the power-semi theme.

companies.name: ASPEED Technology
companies.thesis_note: ~80% of general server BMC chips and ~100% of Nvidia Hopper/Blackwell GPU-rack BMCs (87 per NVL72) — an 'ASML-like' near-monopoly chokepoint. BMC TAM raised to ~65M units by 2030 on AI-server + agentic demand; content/ASP rising. Re-rank candidate (possible conviction-3).
companies.froth_note: BMC duopoly with agentic-era torque; Taiwan momentum money owns it heavily.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.thesis_note: Largest interconnection/colo REIT (~70% colo revenue); Equinix Fabric on-demand interconnect (500k+ interconnects, ~60% of large new contracts AI). The convexity is interconnect, not just floor space — a beneficiary of agentic east-west traffic. Cross-link to Networking.

companies.name: Digital Realty
companies.thesis_note: Major DC REIT; ServiceFabric software-defined interconnect closing the gap to Equinix. Levered to colo demand + AI interconnect. A facility-layer landlord, not a hardware chokepoint.

companies.name: LOTES
companies.thesis_note: ~35% of CPU sockets + memory/quick-disconnect liquid-cooling connectors; content-per-server rising as pin counts go 5,000→7,000+. Now raising prices (vs historical cuts); Vietnam capacity for non-China AI-server supply.

companies.name: FIT Hon Teng
companies.thesis_note: Foxconn interconnect arm; ~40% CPU-socket share + 224G/448G connectivity, high-speed cables, M-CRPS power connectors. Cloud/DC revenue mix climbing ~16% (2025) → low-30s% by 2028.

companies.name: Coherent
companies.thesis_note: Vertically integrated lasers (EML) + transceivers + SiC optics. Nvidia ~$2B supply commitment. Optical chokepoint owner. Also a beneficiary of China's June 2026 InP substrate export easing — broader InP supply unlocks III-V optical capacity. Jul 2026: NVDA/AVGO CPO switches enter volume ramp — optical-engine supply named a key bottleneck; sell-side sizes Coherent's NVDA-linked optical opportunity in the tens of $B. Aug 2026: prime beneficiary of the proposed FCC ban on Chinese transceivers — but the honest caveat (Foundation for American Innovation) is that COHR/LITE lack the scale to replace >50% Chinese share quickly: expect pricing power and shortage before share capture.
companies.froth_note: Optics run has been powerful; EML/datacom tightness real but multiple now assumes it persists.

companies.name: Lumentum
companies.thesis_note: EML/DFB lasers + datacom optics; Nvidia ~$2B commitment locks supply. Leverage to 1.6T + laser scarcity. Also the MEMS-mirror OCS system supplier to Google's TPU pods (Project Apollo, R300/R64) — direct TPU-buildout leverage. Also a beneficiary of China's June 2026 InP substrate export easing — eases its upstream substrate constraint. Jul 2026: Spectrum-X CPO (TSMC COUPE, 400Tb/s) shipping to select partners — the OCS/CPO ecosystem LITE plays in is now in production, not roadmap. Aug 2026: same FCC-ban beneficiary set as COHR, with the same scale caveat — Western vendors cannot absorb Chinese volumes fast. NVDA CPO confirmed in mass production, reinforcing the OCS/CPO optionality.
companies.froth_note: Same optics complex; OCS/CPO optionality partly priced after the run.

companies.name: Fabrinet
companies.thesis_note: Builds transceivers for Nvidia/Cisco/Coherent (first $1B quarter). Thailand-based, geopolitically diversified picks-and-shovels. Aug 2026: Thailand-based optical contract manufacturing is the natural non-China assembly destination if the FCC ban publishes — a quiet, capacity-constrained beneficiary.
companies.froth_note: The natural non-China assembly beneficiary of the transceiver ban, but the market moved on that logic quickly.

companies.name: MACOM Technology
companies.thesis_note: >60% share of 200G photodiodes used in 1.6T modules + TIAs/drivers; architecture-agnostic across pluggable optics, copper-linear and near-packaged optics. A clean 1.6T-transition pick-and-shovel. Aug 2026: photodiode/driver content benefits from any forced re-sourcing away from Chinese transceiver vendors.
companies.froth_note: Photodiode and driver content benefits from re-sourcing; a specialty-RF multiple that already assumes optical wins.

companies.name: Nokia
companies.thesis_note: Via the Infinera buy, owns the only vertically-integrated InP fab in the West (Sunnyvale; CHIPS-backed San Jose/Bethlehem fabs) — ICE-D intra-DC optics vs Lumentum/Coherent. Also a $1B Nvidia 6G investment. A 'forgotten' optics turnaround. Aug 2026: the reshoring winner in optics — $4B committed to US R&D/manufacturing, Nvidia holds a ~$1B stake and partners on CPO, AI sales +49% q/q with optical networks +20%. Directly levered to the FCC's proposed ban on Chinese transceivers.
companies.froth_note: Deep-value telco optics: $4B US commitment, a ~$1B Nvidia stake and 49% AI growth against a stock still 40% off its high.

companies.name: FOCI Fiber Optic
companies.thesis_note: Assembles the fiber-array unit (FAU) for TSMC's COUPE CPO platform (Himax-partnered, Himax holds ~5%); the fiber-to-chip handoff for Nvidia Rubin-era CPO. Small/illiquid (TPEx-listed). Jul 2026: COUPE-based Spectrum-X CPO in volume ramp — FAU attach demand moves from qualification to production phase. Aug 2026 re-rank 1→2: COUPE went volume-production — FAU attach is now shipping revenue, not a qualification story. (Held below 3 pending share-of-wallet proof vs other FAU entrants.) Aug 2026: NVDA CPO confirmed in mass production — FAU attach moves from ramp to run-rate.
companies.froth_note: COUPE FAU attach is now shipping revenue, but a TPEx small-cap that halved is volatile on order timing, not thesis.

companies.name: Ciena
companies.thesis_note: Coherent optical transport + DC interconnect (DCI); acquired Nubis for scale-up/out optics. Levered to the longer-reach links between increasingly distributed AI campuses. Citrini's original optics call. Aug 2026: coherent-optics beneficiary of the proposed Chinese-transceiver import ban; systems exposure makes it a slower-burn winner than the component names.
companies.froth_note: Coherent systems at a systems multiple; a transceiver-ban beneficiary the optics crowd has largely ignored.

companies.name: Furukawa Electric
companies.thesis_note: DFB laser chips (capacity +500% by 2028; Nvidia locked long-term contracts) + MT/MPO ferrules + rollable-ribbon cable + CPO ELS/TOSA modules. Moving up the value chain into CPO light sources.
companies.froth_note: Down ~47% while owning DFB lasers, MT/MPO ferrules and InP — Japanese industrial pricing on a photonics chokepoint.

companies.name: Sumitomo Electric
companies.thesis_note: MT/MPO/MMC ferrules (~30% share) + EML/CW-LD lasers + InP substrates (2.4x capacity by 2028) + fiber-to-chip attach for CPO (FlexBeamGuidE); Nvidia SiPh ecosystem partner. Owns the fiber-to-chip interface.
companies.froth_note: Conglomerate multiple over a genuine optical-components franchise; the CPO content is not in the price.

companies.name: Applied Optoelectronics
companies.thesis_note: 800G/1.6T pluggables (Microsoft-heavy, ~29% of revenue) scaling toward CPO lasers. Demand > supply, but a concentrated/fragile customer base and a heroic CPO ramp — crowded, valuation-sensitive. China's June 2026 InP substrate export easing is a meaningful supply-unlock catalyst for the entire pluggables/CPO laser chain — direct upstream beneficiary. Aug 2026: US-based pluggable transceiver capacity becomes strategically scarce if the FCC ban publishes — the highest-beta way to play forced re-sourcing, with the usual execution/valuation caveats.

companies.name: Sivers Semiconductors
companies.thesis_note: Swedish photonics — InP/GaAs III-V photonic ICs + 5G mmWave RFICs. Direct beneficiary of June 2026 China InP substrate easing. Small-cap pure-play; speculative.

companies.name: Semtech
companies.thesis_note: Industry-leading transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) + laser drivers; acquired HieFo for proven InP lasers/gain chips. Positioning for 1.6T/3.2T + CPO/near-packaged optics. Architecture-agnostic optics-component pick. Aug 2026: TIA/driver and InP content levered to the same forced re-sourcing thesis.

companies.name: InnoLight Technology
companies.thesis_note: World #1 transceiver maker; with Eoptolink ~60% of Nvidia 800G. China assembly dominance — a quiet supply exposure. Aug 2026 RISK: ~27% of the global datacenter-transceiver market (Counterpoint) makes InnoLight the primary target of the FCC's proposed US import ban on new-model Chinese transceivers. US hyperscaler demand is the exposure; still drafting and could be shelved, but this is now the dominant swing factor in the thesis.
companies.froth_note: Valuation is no longer the operative question — the FCC import ban is. Policy, not multiple, decides this one.

companies.name: Eoptolink
companies.thesis_note: Fast-rising 800G/1.6T transceiver maker; gaining Nvidia share. China optical-module growth play. Aug 2026 RISK: second-largest Chinese transceiver vendor — same FCC import-ban exposure as InnoLight.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Electric
companies.thesis_note: One of <5 EML laser makers — the deepest optical chokepoint. Diversified conglomerate; small but strategic laser unit. Also makes MELFA industrial robots + a servo/PLC automation ecosystem — a robotics-adjacent angle.

companies.name: Harmonic Drive Systems
companies.thesis_note: The historic near-monopoly in harmonic (strain-wave) reducers — the compact, high-ratio, zero-backlash gearing that robot joints need and that almost nobody else manufactures at quality. Designed into most Western humanoid platforms, and the qualification cycle for a joint reducer is measured in years. 2026 state: Optimus is ramping at Fremont and supplier orders are turning real, which is why the stock moved 12% in a session in August. Risk: Chinese reducer makers are closing the quality gap on price, and humanoid volume timing remains the theme's central unknown.
companies.froth_note: Harmonic-reducer monopoly but humanoid timing risk means the theme's froth lands here when robotics wobbles.

companies.name: Nabtesco
companies.thesis_note: Roughly 60% of the world's precision cycloidal (RV) reducers — the high-torque counterpart to Harmonic Drive, used where industrial arms and larger humanoid joints carry real load. Same structural position: a precision-machining moat built over decades, qualified into platforms that cannot easily re-engineer around it. 2026 state: rides both the industrial-automation base and the humanoid option, and moved 8% in a session on the August order flow. Risk: industrial robot demand is cyclical, and the humanoid premium can deflate faster than it inflated.
companies.froth_note: RV-reducer chokepoint, same humanoid-narrative sensitivity as Harmonic.

companies.name: THK
companies.thesis_note: Linear motion (ball screws, rails); planetary roller screws are a humanoid bottleneck. Motion-component leader.
companies.froth_note: Industrial ball/roller-screw earnings stand on their own — humanoid volume is upside you are not paying much for.

companies.name: NSK
companies.thesis_note: Bearings + ball/roller screws; humanoid linear-actuation content. Auto-cycle exposed but robotics optionality.

companies.name: Nidec
companies.thesis_note: World's largest motor maker; frameless/BLDC for robotics + EV. Broad motion exposure; China competition rising.
companies.froth_note: Motor scale is real, but self-inflicted execution and governance problems, not valuation, are what the price is arguing about.

companies.name: Inovance
companies.thesis_note: China's motion-control champion vertically integrating motors/drives/screws into humanoids. The China localization core.
companies.froth_note: Best-run Chinese motion-control name; quality is priced, and China industrial demand is the swing factor.

companies.name: Sanhua Intelligent
companies.thesis_note: Exclusive Tier-1 Tesla Optimus actuator assembler ($685M order). The clearest listed Optimus supply-chain proxy.
companies.froth_note: Prices a humanoid-assembly ramp that has barely started — pure Optimus narrative with thermal-management earnings underneath.

companies.name: Tuopu Group
companies.thesis_note: Tesla Optimus 'T-Chain' Tier-1 actuator supplier (alongside Sanhua); auto-parts base (NVH, thermal, chassis) pivoting to humanoid linear/rotary actuators. A second listed Optimus actuator proxy. Jul 2026: humanoid supply-chain stocks surged Jul 10 on Optimus procurement orders as the Fremont line ramp begins — T-chain volume orders turning real.
companies.froth_note: The definitional Optimus-narrative stock: T-Chain orders are real but small against a multiple built on the 2,500/week target.

companies.name: Shuanghuan Driveline
companies.thesis_note: Chinese precision-gear maker pivoting into RV reducers for industrial + humanoid joints (dedicated reducer line). Domestic challenger to Nabtesco on the heavy-joint side.

companies.name: Beite Technology
companies.thesis_note: Shanghai-listed; committed ¥1.85bn to a planetary-roller-screw plant — the costliest, most supply-constrained linear-actuator component. China second-source on the Optimus roller-screw bottleneck.

companies.name: Leaderdrive (Green Harmonic)
companies.thesis_note: China harmonic-reducer leader (绿的谐波 'Leaderdrive'; ~25%+ share); targeting Optimus supply via a 500K-unit/yr plant. STAR-listed localization beneficiary. (NB: same company sometimes mislabeled 'Green Harmonic' vs 'Leaderdrive'.)

companies.name: Fanuc
companies.thesis_note: Industrial robotics 'Big Four'; CNC + arms. Incumbent base; humanoid wave is optionality, China share-loss is risk.

companies.name: Yaskawa Electric
companies.thesis_note: Servo drives + industrial arms; motion-control breadth. Automation + humanoid component optionality.

companies.name: Regal Rexnord
companies.thesis_note: Owns Kollmorgen/Allied Motion frameless torque motors used in humanoids. US motion-component exposure.

companies.name: Schaeffler
companies.thesis_note: Bearings/motion major now selling a full humanoid joint module (gear + bearing + motor, ~€1,500/bot) and courting Figure + Agility; only ~18% China revenue. Citrini's clearest 'non-China humanoid design-win' play. Owns Ewellix (roller screws).
companies.froth_note: Auto/industrial bearings at a value multiple; the humanoid joint-module business is a free call option inside it.

companies.name: Allient
companies.thesis_note: US motion-control platform (ElectroFlux radial / SA axial-flux motors); exited powersport/auto to focus on robotics, defense, medical. Engineering-led OEM motion cores, designing out rare-earth content. Re-rating on the motion supercycle.

companies.name: Wolong Electric
companies.thesis_note: Major global high-power motor maker; motors already used in Unitree robot dogs and applicable to large humanoid hip/knee/shoulder joints. China motor-supply-chain breadth.

companies.name: Ningbo Shuanglin
companies.thesis_note: Auto-supply-chain player scaling roller screws + linear actuators toward ~300K units/yr ahead of Tesla Optimus demand (each Optimus uses ~14 linear actuators). A concrete China scale-production signal.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.thesis_note: Optimus is the humanoid demand-setter — owns both the actuator-BOM design and the embodied-AI stack; Gen-3 reportedly ~70% China-sourced. The program that pulls the entire robotics supply chain. Diversified (auto/energy) = a robotics call-option, not a pure-play. Jul 2026: Optimus Fremont line ramping — ~100-150/wk Jul → target 1,000/wk by Sept, 2,500/wk by year-end (internal use only in 2026); Texas Gigafactory broken ground.
companies.froth_note: Optimus is a story told inside a stock that already trades on stories — the robot line is early and internal-use only through 2026.

companies.name: Hyundai Motor
companies.thesis_note: Owns Boston Dynamics (Atlas) — premier Western humanoid R&D and Citrini's top-scored robotics OEM. Robotics is optionality on a global auto OEM.
companies.froth_note: An automaker at ~5x with Boston Dynamics attached — nearly 50% off its high, you are paid to hold the optionality.

companies.name: UBTech Robotics
companies.thesis_note: Cleanest listed pure-play humanoid maker; in-house servo actuators (0.2–200Nm), Walker S deployed in factories (BYD, Foxconn). China humanoid champion.
companies.froth_note: Pure-play humanoid, loss-making, priced on units it has not shipped. The cleanest expression of the theme and its froth.

companies.name: Xiaomi
companies.thesis_note: CyberOne humanoid + CyberDog quadruped leverage Xiaomi's consumer-electronics + EV ecosystem and cost engineering; a 'de facto humanoid supplier' contender if it scales. Diversified, robotics is optionality.

companies.name: Estun Automation
companies.thesis_note: China industrial-robot + servo/motion-control champion (owns Trio UK, Cloos DE); core components in-house. Humanoid optionality off an industrial-arm base.

companies.name: ABB
companies.thesis_note: IRB industrial-robot family + ABB Robotics AI platform; deep actuator/control/integration stack. 'Big Four' incumbent; humanoid is optionality.

companies.name: Midea Group (KUKA)
companies.thesis_note: Owns KUKA ('Big Four' arms); RMB10bn Guangdong humanoid park. KUKA actuator IP + Midea cost curve = domestic humanoid optionality; diversified appliances base.

companies.name: Kawasaki Heavy Inds.
companies.thesis_note: Major industrial-robot maker (welding/assembly) with in-house servo know-how; Kaleido humanoid program. Diversified heavy-industry base, robotics optionality.

companies.name: Rainbow Robotics
companies.thesis_note: HUBO humanoid developer; Samsung lifted its stake to ~14% to accelerate biped R&D. Korea's Figure/Tesla-style peer with in-house actuation IP. (KOSDAQ-listed.)

companies.name: XPeng
companies.thesis_note: XPeng Robotics' IRON biped backed by a ¥100bn 20-yr commitment; shares EV supply chain + vision stack. China humanoid roll-out play; capital-intensive. (NYSE ADR.)

companies.name: Doosan Robotics
companies.thesis_note: Korean cobot leader and K-Humanoid Alliance member; multi-arm humanoid platform guided for 2026. Cobot base + humanoid optionality.

companies.name: Seiko Epson
companies.thesis_note: #1 SCARA robot maker; proprietary GYROPLUS motion sensing. Precision small-arm kinematics map to humanoid wrists/arms; diversified (printers) base.

companies.name: Teradyne
companies.thesis_note: Owns Universal Robots (cobot leader) + MiR (AMRs); UR arms power Amazon's Vulcan pick/stow robot — a potential $300-400M contract as Amazon automates ~80% of 14B hand-stowed items/yr. Core is semiconductor ATE (Advantest duopoly) + AI/HBM + custom-ASIC test, so robotics is one leg of a dual-catalyst name.
companies.froth_note: Semi-test earnings underpin the valuation; UR cobots and the Amazon Vulcan win are optionality on top.

companies.name: Sony Group
companies.thesis_note: Dominant CMOS image sensors + OLEDoS micro-displays (Apple Vision Pro) + lasers. Multi-vertical sensing/display chokepoint.
companies.froth_note: Image-sensor near-monopoly inside a conglomerate multiple; entertainment earnings mask the franchise.

companies.name: Hesai Group
companies.thesis_note: China lidar cost leader (>1.6M units 2025); Nvidia robotics partner. Fast-commoditizing but volume leader.

companies.name: Keyence
companies.thesis_note: Machine-vision + factory sensor powerhouse, ~50%+ margins. Automation breadth; premium quality compounder.
companies.froth_note: Permanently premium and deservedly so, sitting 4% off its high — quality with no valuation cushion.

companies.name: Cognex
companies.thesis_note: Machine-vision pure-play; logistics + factory automation. Cyclical but robotics/vision secular tailwind.

companies.name: TDK
companies.thesis_note: InvenSense IMUs (ICM-42688 widely used in humanoids) + passives + batteries. Broad sensing/components exposure.

companies.name: Novanta
companies.thesis_note: Owns ATI 6-axis force/torque sensors — key to dexterous manipulation. Precision-sensing niche exposure.

companies.name: Keli Sensing
companies.thesis_note: China's largest traditional sensor maker, expanding into multi-axis (6-way) torque sensing for robot wrists/ankles — competing with ATI (Novanta) + Sunrise. Fills the force/torque chokepoint that gates dexterous manipulation.
companies.froth_note: Fills the force/torque gap, but Chinese small-cap sensor pricing moves with the humanoid narrative cycle.

companies.name: Allegro MicroSystems
companies.thesis_note: Hall-effect + current + magnetic position sensor ICs — 'in every joint' for precise motion control; sizes the humanoid-robot sensor SAM at >$10B (2030-35) with auto/robotics/DC cross-sell. Automotive-cycle exposed.

companies.name: Apex Dynamics
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan's #1 planetary gearbox maker — ships >450K/yr globally, second only to Germany's Wittenstein. Used in semi foundries, EV plants, food/beverage. Lower-cost rotary workhorse vs harmonic/RV — fits lower-cost humanoid joints.

companies.name: Timken
companies.thesis_note: Industrial bearings; owns Spinea, which ships ultra-compact cycloidal reducers viable for humanoid joints. US motion-component diversification play with humanoid optionality.

companies.name: Han's Laser
companies.thesis_note: Han's Laser — China industrial-automation conglomerate (laser-cell + Elfin cobots + 3D inspection). Cited as a Chinese motor/cobot challenger; humanoid integration optionality off a diversified automation base.

companies.name: Kinco Electric
companies.thesis_note: China frameless / servo motor challenger to Kollmorgen and Nidec; named alongside VEICHI and Han's as the China motor cohort. STAR-listed motion-control localization play.

companies.name: Hota Industrial
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan precision-gear maker — sits alongside Apex Dynamics as the Taiwan planetary-gearbox cohort; Tesla/Optimus drivetrain optionality given the supply-chain shift away from China.

companies.name: RBC Bearings
companies.thesis_note: US precision bearings maker; named alongside Schaeffler and Timken as the Western bearing cohort. Defense-budget tailwind + humanoid optionality; not a pure-play.

companies.name: Cloudflare
companies.chain_layer: CDN + Workers + agentic infra (zero-trust, pay-per-crawl, x402)
companies.thesis_note: Most comprehensive agentic-infra play: Workers (distributed compute), Durable Objects (state), pay-per-crawl, NET-dollar stablecoin for agentic commerce, Browser Rendering, signed agent traffic, Firewall for AI. Citrini June: 'beat + guide raise + 20% headcount cut, sold off' — still bullish on quality + exposure.
companies.froth_note: Sitting at its 52-week high on the agentic-traffic narrative — the richest multiple in this vertical, priced for the story landing.

companies.name: Akamai
companies.thesis_note: CDN pivoting to AI compute (Akamai Inference Cloud Oct 2025, $250M capex). API security +100% YoY. Citrini June: $1.8B 7-yr frontier-lab compute commitment; +80% YTD. The CDN-to-compute-delivery thesis.
companies.froth_note: Legacy-CDN expectations are on the floor; any AI-delivery traction is upside nobody is paying for.

companies.name: Fastly
companies.thesis_note: Edge compute + AI Accelerator (semantic caching cuts inference cost/latency). WebAssembly Compute platform. Citrini June: security +47%, compute +67%, RPO +63%. Highest convexity among CDNs.

companies.name: Twilio
companies.thesis_note: CPaaS for agents: ConversationRelay (out-of-the-box voice AI), Segment (15-yr customer-data moat), A2H protocol. Already handles 85% of own inbound sales via AI. Citrini June: trades >30x fwd.
companies.froth_note: Voice-agent demand is genuine, but the multiple re-rated on it before the revenue showed up.

companies.name: Bandwidth
companies.thesis_note: Owns physical telephony infrastructure (PSTN interconnects, carrier licenses, number portability) in 60+ countries; rented by MSFT/GOOG/AMZN. OpenAI Realtime API integration. Citrini June: up ~300%; won Salesforce Agentforce contract.
companies.froth_note: Owns real last-mile telephony assets; small-cap fragility, not valuation, is the risk that bites.

companies.name: Sinch
companies.thesis_note: Swedish CPaaS un-rerated catch-up to TWLO/BAND. EU AI Act August 2026 reasoning-log requirement could be a regulatory tailwind. Smaller / cheaper exposure to the same agentic-comms wave.

companies.name: SailPoint
companies.thesis_note: Identity governance lifecycle — provisions and revokes access for every identity (human + non-human + AI agent). Citrini June: ~11% of governed identities are already non-human; platformization angle vs PANW's CyberArk acquisition.

companies.name: Palo Alto Networks
companies.thesis_note: Platformization: Chronosphere acq (observability) + CyberArk acq (~$25B, PAM/agent identity). Zero Standing Privilege architecture for agentic workflows. Citrini's preferred cyber-platform play for the agentic era.
companies.froth_note: At its high on the platformization narrative — quality business, no margin of safety in the price.

companies.name: Datadog
companies.thesis_note: Observability for monitoring + billing of ephemeral agent workloads. Citrini June: non-AI segment +25%; upgraded view post-earnings. Telemetry IS financial plumbing in agent-native architectures.
companies.froth_note: At its high; agentic-observability is a real tailwind already fully reflected in a premium SaaS multiple.

companies.name: Dynatrace
companies.thesis_note: Observability + AIOps platform. Healthy print; Citrini June names it as a second observability pick alongside DDOG.

companies.name: JFrog
companies.thesis_note: DevOps platformization → unified dev environment incl. model/artifact registry. Reference designs for AI-native dev. Citrini June: noted as DevOps platformization play.

companies.name: VeriSign
companies.thesis_note: Authoritative .com/.net registry — 450B DNS queries/day. Every agent web request starts with DNS resolution; agentic workflows fan out to 10 lookups vs 1 for human. 67% operating margins, virtually zero CAC.

companies.name: A10 Networks
companies.thesis_note: Manages the (now-scarce) IPv4 address table via NAT (Thunder CGN) + builds IPv6 transition infrastructure. Every persistent agent session needs an addressable endpoint. Cybersecurity wrapper growing.

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.thesis_note: Neocloud — $99.4B RPO Q1 2026, 1GW+ active capacity. $21B Meta expansion, $6B Jane Street cloud commitment + $1B equity. Citrini June: missed Q2 guide ('supply constrained and operationally difficult') — caution flag despite the demand.
companies.froth_note: GPU renter squeezed between inference-price deflation and $B lease obligations; Q2 supply-constrained miss was the tell.

companies.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
companies.thesis_note: Server systems + Juniper acq (networking +152% YoY). HPE Private Cloud full-stack subscription. Picks up agentic on-prem demand.

companies.name: DigitalOcean
companies.thesis_note: Managed cloud for SMBs / digital-native AI startups. High-touch partner vs hyperscalers' DIY. Re-accelerating topline as DNE/agentic-startup mix climbs.

companies.name: Jabil
companies.thesis_note: Diversified EMS; Intelligent Infrastructure segment (robotics capital equipment + AI servers) led recent upside. Citrindex Robotics basket member; broader AI-server EMS exposure alongside CLS.

companies.name: Huber+Suhner
companies.thesis_note: OCS + RF connectivity; record CHF432M backlog; scaling Polish capacity 5x. Critical player alongside Lumentum in Google's MEMS OCS / Project Apollo TPU pods. EU Chips Act 2.0 beneficiary.
companies.froth_note: Swiss industrial pricing on the OCS/interconnect optionality; nobody is paying an AI premium for this.

companies.name: Canatu
companies.thesis_note: Sole CNT pellicle pure-play; ASML supplier (CNT pellicles needed for High-NA EUV reticle protection). ~€300M cap, ~€15M TTM revenue — high risk / high reward. EU Chips Act 2.0 microcap.

companies.name: Nordic Semiconductor
companies.thesis_note: Only EU fabless low-power wireless pure-play; Bluetooth LE ~40% share. Edge-AI SoCs for IoT/wearables (the on-device inference inflection's silicon supplier). EU Chips Act 2.0 beneficiary.
companies.froth_note: Edge-connectivity content is real; a Nordic small-cap whose multiple assumes IoT recovery.

companies.name: Infineon
companies.thesis_note: European power-semi major; SiC + silicon power for auto + AI 800V-HVDC. Prior EU Chips Act 1.0 winner; positioned for 2.0. Acquired AMS-OSRAM sensor unit (€570M).
companies.froth_note: The power-semi share leader priced as a cyclical automotive supplier — the datacenter power story is not in the multiple.

companies.name: Schneider Electric
companies.thesis_note: French power-management major; named as 800V HVDC AI-DC beneficiary alongside Eaton + Siemens. Diversified industrial-power exposure.
companies.froth_note: Quality compounder trading near its high; the AI-electrification thesis is understood and paid for.

companies.name: Eaton
companies.thesis_note: Power-management major; SST (solid-state transformer) entrant via Resilient Power acquisition (~$150M, 2025). 800V HVDC beneficiary; named in both Citrini's Supply Chain Inheritance and the June 2026 800V power-conversion thesis (Q3 2026 first volume shipments).
companies.froth_note: At its 52-week high as the crowd's favourite AI-electrification proxy — the fundamentals are excellent and entirely reflected.

companies.name: Siemens
companies.thesis_note: German industrial + power-systems major. Multi-segment AI-infra exposure: Siemens Digital Industries (automation) + Siemens Energy spin-off (grid/HVDC) + Siemens EDA (#3 chip-design software). 800V HVDC + EU Chips Act 2.0 + EDA cross-cutting.
companies.froth_note: A conglomerate where AI datacenter demand is a slice, not the story; you are not paying an AI multiple here.

companies.name: Song Chuan Precision
companies.thesis_note: Taiwan relay maker (electromechanical + safety + HVDC + magnetic-latching). Pivoting into HVDC, liquid-cooling, AI-server energy-storage. Direct beneficiary — Q3 2026 first volume shipments flagged for Nvidia Vera Rubin + Google next-gen DCs.

companies.name: Silicon Motion
companies.thesis_note: Flash controller specialist — central to the 'past the DRAM tax' thesis (controller optimization is one of 3 paths to offload weight storage from scarce DRAM to NAND/HBF). Edge-AI memory controller content rising.

companies.name: Ouster
companies.thesis_note: Rev8/L4 silicon color LiDAR; Nvidia Jetson/DRIVE integration. SPAD-SoC architecture — robotics + autonomy. Citrini's preferred LiDAR pure-play alongside Hesai.

companies.name: Aeva Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Atlas 4D LiDAR — frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW). Daimler Truck Level-4 road tests; Torc partnership targeting 2027 series production. Differentiated 4D physics vs ToF lidar.

companies.name: Axcelis Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Ion implantation tools — pivotal for SiC doping (the EV-cohort capacity now inheriting AI 800V-HVDC demand). Mid-merger with Veeco (VECO).

companies.name: Power Integrations
companies.thesis_note: High-voltage power-conversion ICs; AC-to-DC + DC-DC conversion. AI rack power transition (800V HVDC) demand; Citrindex Dynamic AI basket member.

companies.name: Sunny Optical
companies.thesis_note: China's largest optical lens + camera module maker — smartphones, autos, AR/VR, robotics. Multi-vertical optics exposure including robotics-vision angle. Citrindex Robotics basket member.

companies.name: Victory Giant Technology
companies.thesis_note: High-layer-count PCB maker for AI servers — sits at the AI-server BOM intersection of CCL + HVLP copper foil. Citrindex Dynamic AI basket. China PCB ascent.

companies.name: Silex Microsystems
companies.thesis_note: Swedish pure-play MEMS foundry (now owned by Sai MicroElectronics 300456.SZ). Fabs the MEMS mirror chips Lumentum uses in Google's TPU OCS pods. EU Chips Act 2.0 + photonics enabler crossover.

companies.name: Ambiq Micro
companies.thesis_note: Sub-threshold ultra-low-power MCUs — sips microamps. Critical for always-on AI sensing at the battery-constrained edge (wearables, hearables, medical patches).

companies.name: Sensata Technologies
companies.thesis_note: Industrial pressure / position / temperature / current sensors. Broad sensing portfolio with robotics + automation cross-sell. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Synaptics
companies.thesis_note: Touch / fingerprint / display-driver / audio ICs. IoT + edge-AI human-interface SoCs. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Knowles
companies.thesis_note: MEMS microphones + balanced armature speakers + specialty capacitors. Voice-AI hardware angle + hearable / earbud content. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: Arteris
companies.thesis_note: Network-on-Chip (NoC) interconnect IP — sits inside SoC designs from custom-ASIC / robotics-silicon designers. License-based recurring revenue. Citrindex Robotics basket.

companies.name: CEVA
companies.thesis_note: Licensable DSP, AI, Bluetooth/5G IP for edge SoCs. Royalties per shipped chip. Citrindex Dynamic AI basket.

companies.name: Intuitive Surgical
companies.thesis_note: Surgical robotics leader; razor-razorblade installed base. Adjacent end-market for precision robotics.

companies.name: Hamamatsu Photonics
companies.thesis_note: Japan's photodetector leader (photodiodes, SiPM/SPAD, PMTs) — receivers for lidar + machine-vision + medical/industrial sensing. A quiet photonics-sensing chokepoint across robotics, autonomy and instrumentation.

companies.name: Analog Devices
companies.thesis_note: High-end MEMS IMUs (ADIS) + precision analog/signal-chain and ToF sensing front-ends for robots, industrial and autos. Broad, high-quality exposure across the robot nervous system.
companies.froth_note: Best-in-class analog franchise carrying a persistent quality premium — nothing here is cheap.

companies.name: Orbbec
companies.thesis_note: China 3D-vision specialist — structured-light + ToF depth cameras for robots/embodied AI (Nvidia robotics-ecosystem partner). Depth perception for manipulation + navigation.

companies.name: Melexis
companies.thesis_note: Belgian magnetic/Hall position + current sensor specialist — joint-position and motor-commutation sensing for robots and autos. Automotive-cycle exposed; robotics optionality.

companies.name: Ambarella
companies.thesis_note: Edge-AI vision/perception SoCs (CVflow). Used in robotics + ADAS + drones. Cited alongside Broadcom/MediaTek/Marvell as a candidate for fixed-function VLA ASICs as embodied AI matures. Smaller pure-play exposure to robot/edge inference.

companies.name: Himax Technologies
companies.thesis_note: LCoS micro-displays + display driver ICs. Hidden CPO play: makes the nanoimprint optics-block/micro-lens-array inside the fiber-array unit for TSMC COUPE (with FOCI) — a Nvidia Rubin-era ramp. Also the likely Apple smart-glasses supplier (WiseEye low-power sensing, LCoS, WLO waveguides). Non-driver segment is the growth vector. Jul 2026: CPO mass production begins (TrendForce) — wafer-level-optics/FAU content for COUPE now shipping in volume.
companies.froth_note: CPO and smart-glasses content are real, but a small-cap that moves 40% on single design-win headlines carries its own risk.

companies.name: BOE Technology
companies.thesis_note: China display giant scaling OLEDoS + microLED for MR/AR. Volume + cost; China display ascendancy play.

companies.name: AU Optronics
companies.thesis_note: Panel maker pivoting to microLED + automotive/AR. Taiwan display transition exposure.

companies.name: ams OSRAM
companies.thesis_note: microLED + emitters + optical sensing. AR/automotive photonics; restructuring story with microLED optionality.

companies.name: MicroVision
companies.thesis_note: Laser beam scanning + lidar. Speculative AR/automotive display-tech option; high risk.

companies.name: Corning
companies.thesis_note: High-index glass for AR waveguides + optical fiber for AI clusters. Materials chokepoint bordering the hard-assets map.
companies.froth_note: The Nvidia- and Amazon-underwritten US optical expansion has been discovered by the market; a good business now carrying an AI premium.

companies.name: Vuzix
companies.thesis_note: Waveguide manufacturer + enterprise AR OEM; acquired ex-Google waveguide lab. Speculative AR pure-play.

companies.name: Qualcomm
companies.thesis_note: De-facto AR/XR SoC (Snapdragon AR) — the smart-glasses compute chokepoint. Diversified; AR is the call-option.
companies.froth_note: Trades on handset cycles at a single-digit-ish multiple — the AR/XR SoC franchise is nearly free.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.thesis_note: Ray-Ban Display breakout + Orion; the AI-glasses category creator + biggest AR R&D spender. Drives the whole AR BOM.
companies.froth_note: Priced as an AI-capex spender first and an AR device OEM second; the glasses business is a small part of what you buy.

companies.name: Goertek
companies.thesis_note: Built the Ray-Ban Display light engine; dominant AR/VR device assembler. China assembly chokepoint for smart glasses.
companies.froth_note: Assembly economics with AR/VR optionality; margins depend on customers who can dual-source.

companies.name: Luxshare Precision
companies.thesis_note: Major Apple/AR device assembler + components. China precision-assembly leverage to AR/wearables ramp.

companies.name: SICC (Tianyue)
companies.thesis_note: SiC substrates; emerging SiC AR waveguides (Meta Orion). Verify ticker. Speculative materials-chokepoint option.

companies.name: Murata Manufacturing
companies.thesis_note: World #1 MLCC. An AI accelerator board carries an order of magnitude more capacitor content than a standard server — passives are the invisible BOM inflation of the buildout. The quality name in the layer the MS value-chain map files under server components.
companies.froth_note: Down ~40% while AI boards consume an order of magnitude more MLCC content — the passives inflation is not priced.

companies.name: Taiyo Yuden
companies.thesis_note: MLCC top-3, strong in high-capacitance server grades. Rides the same AI passive-content wave as Murata with more consumer-mix drag.

companies.name: Yageo
companies.thesis_note: Passives roll-up (KEMET, Pulse, Ferroxcube). More commodity-tilted than the Japanese duo — the beta way to play AI passive content.

companies.name: Lite-On Technology
companies.thesis_note: #2 AI-server power supply behind Delta; power shelves + 48V architectures for GB-class racks, same 800V-HVDC runway at a valuation discount to Delta.
companies.froth_note: Only ~8% off its high on the 800V-DC and Bailly CPO wins; the re-rating has largely happened.

companies.name: Auras Technology
companies.thesis_note: Cold plates, manifolds and CDUs into NVDA GB-class racks — one of the purest listed liquid-cooling component plays; capacity constrained through 2026. Complements AVC (have) in the layer.
companies.froth_note: Cold-plate capacity is genuinely constrained, but the market found this name early and priced the constraint.

companies.name: Sunon (Sunonwealth)
companies.thesis_note: Server-fan and thermal-module franchise — every air-cooled rack still ships a wall of its fans. Watch item: how much fan content the liquid transition strands.

companies.name: Sanyo Denki
companies.thesis_note: San Ace fans are the Japanese quality benchmark in server cooling; steady datacenter content growth, not explosive AI torque.

companies.name: Wistron
companies.thesis_note: Assembles NVDA GPU modules and baseboards upstream of Dell/SMCI system integration — among the largest direct AI-server revenue ramps in Taiwan. Completes our ODM set alongside Wiwynn, Quanta, Hon Hai.
companies.froth_note: At its high on GPU-baseboard volume — an assembler's economics carrying a growth-stock multiple.

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.thesis_note: AI-server brand share leader (xAI, CoreWeave builds; multi-$B backlog). Revenue torque with thin server margins — weak value capture vs the component chokepoints upstream.

companies.name: Hitachi (Hitachi Energy)
companies.thesis_note: Hitachi Energy is a top-2 global transformer + HVDC franchise; multi-year transformer lead times are the physical bottleneck between AI datacenter demand and the grid.
companies.froth_note: Hitachi Energy's transformer backlog is the crown jewel; the conglomerate has re-rated substantially on it already.

companies.name: Siemens Energy
companies.thesis_note: Grid-technology near-duopoly with Hitachi Energy — transformer and switchgear backlogs stretch years — plus large gas turbines for behind-the-meter DC power.
companies.froth_note: Grid-technology duopoly economics, now widely understood after a very large multi-year run.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
companies.thesis_note: Top-3 gas-turbine maker (with GE Vernova, Siemens Energy); turbine slots for datacenter behind-the-meter power are effectively sold out years forward. Japan nuclear-restart optionality on top.
companies.froth_note: Turbine slots sold out years forward and the market knows; Japan nuclear-restart optionality is the un-priced part.

companies.name: Cummins
companies.thesis_note: Datacenter genset standard — backup-power content scales with every MW built. Diversified truck-engine base dilutes the AI signal.

companies.name: Constellation Energy
companies.thesis_note: Largest US nuclear fleet; hyperscaler PPAs (Microsoft / Crane restart) make it the contractual way to own AI power demand rather than the narrative way.
companies.froth_note: Hyperscaler PPAs make it contractual, but the nuclear-premium re-rate already happened.

companies.name: Vistra
companies.thesis_note: Behind-the-fence power via nuclear/gas fleet — the market's favorite AI-power torque trade. High-beta narrative name; Froth Monitor discipline applies. CEG is the contracted alternative.
companies.froth_note: Trades on the AI-power narrative, not contracts — the froth thermometer of the power layer.

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.thesis_note: Fuel cells solve time-to-power: onsite generation beats a multi-year interconnect queue. Real AI datacenter wins now; margin/execution history argues for small sizing.
companies.froth_note: Time-to-power story is real; margins and dilution history say the stock runs ahead of the business.

companies.name: Nebius Group
companies.thesis_note: Neocloud #2 to CoreWeave (ex-Yandex, US-listed); Microsoft and Meta capacity deals. Carries the same inference-price-deflation margin risk the Froth Monitor flags for GPU renters.
companies.froth_note: Same neocloud economics as CRWV with a shorter track record.

companies.name: Amphenol
companies.thesis_note: The #1 interconnect house — backplane connectors, near-chip I/O and power connectors riddle every AI rack, and content per rack rises with each speed generation (112G→224G). Duopoly-ish with TEL at the high end; diversified base (mil/aero, auto) cushions the cycle. The connector layer was the map's biggest unrecorded gap.
companies.froth_note: Quality interconnect compounder within 3% of its high — content growth is real and fully appreciated.

companies.name: TE Connectivity
companies.thesis_note: The other half of the high-end connector duopoly; AI datacenter interconnect is its fastest-growing line but sits inside a large auto/industrial base — APH is the purer AI play, TEL the value way in.

companies.name: nVent Electric
companies.thesis_note: Liquid-cooling manifolds/CDUs and the electrical enclosures + power-distribution gear around AI racks — a smaller, cheaper picks-and-shovels next to Vertiv with rising DC mix.

companies.name: AT&S
companies.thesis_note: Europe's only ABF-substrate maker at scale — Kulim (Malaysia) and Leoben ramps qualified into AI accelerator substrates. Completes an otherwise all-Asia substrate row (Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Nan Ya, SEMCO) with an EU-diversification angle. Balance-sheet-stretched from the capex cycle — the risk side of the thesis.

companies.name: Entegris
companies.thesis_note: Every wafer start consumes its filters, membranes, specialty coatings and ultra-pure handling components — a consumables annuity on fab utilisation rather than fab capex, which makes it less cyclical than the tool makers it sits beside. Purity requirements tighten with each node, so content per wafer rises structurally. The clearest single omission from this map until now.
companies.froth_note: Priced as a cyclical semiconductor consumable rather than an AI beneficiary; the content-per-wafer escalator is not in the multiple.

companies.name: Rambus
companies.chain_layer: Memory interface IP — HBM controllers & PHY
companies.thesis_note: Licenses the controller and PHY IP that lets processors talk to HBM, plus DDR5 register clock drivers — a royalty position inside the memory chokepoint the dashboard cares most about. Every HBM generation transition is a re-licensing event; HBM4's triple qualification means more distinct customers implementing more distinct stacks.
companies.froth_note: The HBM royalty story is understood and the multiple reflects it; execution risk is low, valuation cushion is thin.

companies.name: Advanced Energy Industries
companies.chain_layer: RF & DC power delivery for process tools
companies.thesis_note: Supplies the precision power systems inside etch and deposition chambers — the layer this map already prizes in VAT and MKS. Plasma process control is increasingly the yield variable at advanced nodes, and the qualification cycle with each tool maker is long enough to be a moat.
companies.froth_note: Real content growth plus a datacenter power side-business; the market has already noticed both.

companies.name: Ultra Clean Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Builds the gas-delivery and fluid subsystems that tool makers design around. Genuine WFE leverage, but as an outsourced subassembly partner it captures thin margins and carries customer-concentration risk — the volume way to own the tool cycle, not the profitable way.
companies.froth_note: Highly cyclical, thin margins; moves with WFE sentiment more than with its own economics.

companies.name: Ichor Holdings
companies.thesis_note: Direct peer to Ultra Clean in outsourced fluid-delivery subsystems for Lam and Applied. Same leverage to the tool cycle, same thin-margin structural position — held at monitor level for that reason.
companies.froth_note: A WFE beta instrument; the multiple tracks the tool cycle rather than any durable advantage.

companies.name: Nova
companies.thesis_note: Israeli optical-metrology specialist measuring film thickness and composition inside the process flow. Metrology intensity rises with every added layer and with HBM stacking, and the installed-base service annuity compounds — completes a layer where the map already holds KLA and Onto.
companies.froth_note: Quality metrology franchise that has re-rated with the HBM stacking story; earnings are real, the discount is gone.

companies.name: Camtek
companies.thesis_note: Inspection systems aimed squarely at advanced packaging and HBM — bump, wafer-level and panel inspection, exactly where defect economics are worst because a failed stack destroys several good dies at once. Levered to packaging capacity adds rather than front-end capex.
companies.froth_note: The purest listed inspection play on advanced packaging; that clarity is priced.

companies.name: Nan Ya PCB
companies.thesis_note: Completes the ABF substrate supplier set beside Ibiden, Unimicron, SEMCO and AT&S. Substrates have been a named bottleneck through the whole AI build-out and capacity adds are slow, capital-heavy and qualification-gated; Nan Ya carries the Formosa group's scale behind it.
companies.froth_note: Trades on the Taiwanese PCB cycle rather than the AI substrate shortage — a discount to the constraint it actually supplies into.

companies.name: Legrand
companies.thesis_note: Supplies the power distribution units, busways and rack electrical infrastructure inside the datacenter white space. Datacenter is now the fastest-growing segment of an otherwise steady building-products business — real AI exposure, diluted by the rest of the company.
companies.froth_note: Quality compounder where the datacenter mix has been discovered; the building-products base caps both the upside and the drawdown.

companies.name: Munters Group
companies.thesis_note: Swedish air-treatment and cooling specialist with a fast-growing datacenter division, including evaporative and hybrid systems for high-density halls. A credible European alternative to the Vertiv/nVent axis, though smaller and with a legacy dehumidification base attached.
companies.froth_note: Datacenter growth is genuine but sits inside a mixed industrial; the market rates the whole, not the segment.

companies.name: Capstone Energy+
companies.thesis_note: Microturbine maker rebranded from Capstone Green Energy, pitching itself as a behind-the-meter power platform. The AI hook is real and specific: an 800 VDC microturbine in development aimed at AI datacenters, which lines up with the same 800V rack transition Delta, Infineon and Navitas sell into — a generator that outputs at rack voltage skips conversion stages. The turnaround is also real: FY2026 revenue +24% to $106M, gross margin 32% from 27%, two consecutive quarters of positive net income after emerging from Chapter 11. But it owns no chokepoint — microturbines are contested by reciprocating engines (Cummins, Caterpillar), fuel cells (Bloom) and large gas turbines (GE Vernova, MHI, Siemens Energy) — and the unit scale (65kW–1MW) is an awkward fit for datacenters wanting tens to hundreds of MW, so the role is bridge power and modular CHP rather than primary generation.
companies.froth_note: A $381M OTC Pink micro-cap re-rating on an AI-power narrative two years after Chapter 11. The 800 VDC product is a development programme, not revenue. Listing venue alone rules it out for many mandates.
